title: On the Efficacy of Surface Codes in Compensating for Radiation Events in Superconducting Devices
problem: Radiation-induced faults in superconducting qubits threaten large-scale quantum computer reliability and can undermine the effectiveness of quantum error correction codes due to their persistent nature and area-of-effect characteristics. Current understanding of how surface codes compensate for these radiation-induced faults remains incomplete.
motivation: As technological improvements to qubit stability plateau, understanding and optimizing quantum error correction codes against radiation effects is essential for enabling reliable large-scale quantum computing and practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors ran over 400 million simulations of radiation-induced faults in a surface code—a technique for detecting and correcting errors in quantum computers. They varied four factors: how strong the error correction is, what role each physical qubit plays in the code, how qubits are physically connected to each other, and the energies of the radiation particles. By measuring how these factors affect fault correction, they mapped out how real qubit errors translate into errors in the protected data.
key_novelty: Selecting and tuning the surface code without extra resources can increase radiation fault correction success by up to 10%, providing design guidelines for future quantum error correction systems.
contributions: Comprehensive fault injection study with 400+ million injections characterizing surface code resilience to radiation-induced faults
Systematic analysis of how code distance, qubit roles, topology, and particle energy affect radiation-induced logical error rates
Demonstration that surface code tuning alone yields up to 10% improvement in radiation fault correction capability without overhead
Design guidelines and recommendations for developing future QEC codes with enhanced radiation resilience

metrics.accuracy: physical-to-logical error rates, radiation fault correction probability improvement (up to 10%)

limitations: Validation limited to simulation-based fault injection; practical deployment on real quantum hardware and cost-benefit analysis of tuning overhead not discussed.
primary_theme: quantum error correction for radiation resilience
